comparator.name: Communication and Information Studies
comparator.route: Regular English-taught programme; Humane AI and Digital Society Year 1 option
comparator.sourceNotes: The September 2026 curriculum is a 180-EC programme: 60 EC in each year. Year 1 has 50 EC of named CIS work plus one 10-EC faculty-wide choice; Humane AI and Digital Society is selected because it is listed first, independently of UCR fit. Year 2 contains 50 EC of named CIS work plus a 10-EC faculty-wide course. Year 3 contains a 30-EC minor and 30 EC of CIS work, including a 10-EC thesis and research seminar. The regulations govern the redesigned curriculum; the public programme page still labels its displayed course overview as 2025–2026.

routeSelection.route: Regular English-taught programme; Humane AI and Digital Society Year 1 option
routeSelection.basis: The target includes English and Dutch offerings but no language track. The regular English programme is the default international presentation; the Dutch track changes language for specified units rather than the 180-EC structure. Humane AI and Digital Society is the first-listed Year 1 option.

alternatives.label: Communication, discourse & media
alternatives.labelReason: The schedule integrates rhetoric, language and meaning, media analysis, mixed methods, persuasion, societal context and communication practice.
alternatives.concept: The closest feasible UCR response joins rhetorical and persuasive communication with media, discourse, social context and qualitative and quantitative research. It reflects the programme's breadth without claiming its dedicated workplace, health or thesis sequence.
progression: Communication, media, sociology and methods foundations precede advanced persuasion, discourse, social theory and research. All prerequisites and offerings pass; eight 300-level courses are included.

alternatives.label: Organisational, intercultural & health communication
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum concentrates on communication in organisations and diverse social settings, persuasion, leadership, marketing, health and intervention research.
alternatives.concept: This related direction develops communication in corporate, intercultural, health and leadership settings through social psychology, diversity, marketing, organisational behaviour, psycholinguistics and applied research.
progression: Research, rhetoric, psychology and sociology foundations precede organisational, health, diversity, marketing and psycholinguistic work. All prerequisites and offerings pass; seven 300-level courses are included.
alternatives.distinctness: More than four courses differ from the closest route through business, leadership, health-psychology, diversity, marketing and psycholinguistics work.

alternatives.label: Digital, social-media & AI communication
alternatives.labelReason: The schedule combines media and persuasion with data, AI ethics, digital transformation, social media, marketing and advanced computational analysis.
alternatives.concept: This related direction examines communication shaped by digital platforms and AI, combining media analysis, social psychology and persuasion with data science, responsible AI, digital strategy, marketing and research.
progression: Programming, mathematics, data, media, psychology and methods foundations precede machine learning, social-media analysis, deep learning, persuasion and AI decision systems. All prerequisites and offerings pass; seven 300-level courses are included.
alternatives.distinctness: This route differs substantially from both others through sustained programming, mathematics, data science, machine learning, AI ethics and digital transformation.

blocks: Both develop audience-aware persuasion and argumentation; the Groningen unit is broader and twice the UCR load.
Style & Meaning analyses how linguistic choices shape meaning, without the full cognitive emphasis.
Psycholinguistics addresses language processing and interaction through a cognitive lens.
Media Archaeology studies material properties and cultural effects of communication technologies.
From T.V. to TikTok examines platform narratives and mediated social meaning.
Media & the Environment examines communication framing societal problems and public action.
Leadership Communication addresses communication in organisations, with a narrower leadership focus.
Sociology supplies social and cultural context but is not a dedicated intercultural course.
Medical & Health Psychology covers health behaviour and intervention contexts.
Modern Sociology examines language and communication within changing social contexts.
Personal & Professional Development includes academic writing, presenting and research-question formation.
Qualitative Research Methodology develops design, collection and interpretation for social meaning.
Market Research applies data collection and analysis without reproducing the full communication-specific course.
Statistics & Experimental Methods supplies empirical analysis and experimental design.
Research Methods & Statistics develops design and evaluation across surveys and experiments.
Digital communication, data and responsible AI
AI Ethics examines fairness, privacy, accountability and human interaction with AI.
Required faculty-wide space has no single fixed disciplinary counterpart.
The 30-EC minor is genuine open space; UCR schedules are complete examples.
No scheduled UCR course reproduces Literacy in Society.
Groningen requires a 10-EC CIS thesis and seminar; UCR optional independent research is shown separately.
No scheduled UCR course reproduces the integrated 10-EC CIS Case Study.

selection.assessment: The closest route covers communication, discourse, media and mixed methods. Corporate, intercultural and health strands support an applied-organisational route; digital, social-media, human-computer and responsible-AI interests support a digital route. All are coherent, feasible and pairwise differ by substantially more than four courses.

core: Human communication through language, images, interaction and context
Media narratives, visual communication and digital platforms
Corporate, intercultural, health and societal communication
Qualitative and quantitative research, intervention design and evaluation
adjacent: Digital, social-media, human-computer and AI communication
questions: How do language, images and interaction create meaning across contexts?
How do persuasion, narratives and platforms shape attitudes and public life?
How can communication interventions be designed and evaluated responsibly?

notes.text: Groningen has dedicated text-and-interaction, communication-methods, workplace and health communication, design, literacy, case-study and thesis sequences. UCR assembles strong related liberal-arts pathways but does not reproduce that integrated professional and research sequence.
The 2026–2027 regulations introduce a redesigned curriculum for September 2026 starters. Transitional tables for older cohorts were not used.
